# SPD-009 — Protocol edits in Spud's own files for the CLI era

## Brief
`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/agents/spudagent.md`, `ledger/_templates/ticket.md`, `ledger/_templates/spudagent.md` and the brief template describe file edits, `date`, and counting files. Once [[SPD-007]] and [[SPD-008]] land they must describe `spud` commands instead: the qualified description `SPUD-nnn/Name (id, persona)`; `run_in_background: true` as the default for every spudagent spawn; deliverable globs recorded at `spud member new`; the absolute CLI path; the `permissions.allow` rule for the CLI (background subagents cannot answer prompts); the finishing rule that `SubagentStop` holds a child for (Result or Blocked through the CLI before returning); the `planned` member status. Evidence: the mapping section of the spike; CLAUDE.md protocol steps 1 to 7.

Decided by Eric, 2026-09-12: fan-out limits count children alive at once, so "up to N sub-agents" becomes "up to N alive at once" and a finished or failed child frees its slot (question 3); descriptions carry the team key and background is the spawn default (question 5); refusals from day one (question 6). Lands with [[SPD-007]] and [[SPD-008]].

Done when: the three documents and the templates agree with the CLI, and a ticket run after the cutover shows a team that used only `spud` commands.

Inputs from [[SPD-008]] (Desiree's Result, 2026-09-12): the canonical form is `spud --as <agent_id> member result|log|block …` (`--as` and `--json` are accepted anywhere; the hold and the Stop reason use this order); the first allow reserves a planned row, so after a harness-failed spawn the parent finishes that row as failed and plans a new one, never re-issuing the same description; `SessionStart` matchers stay `startup|resume|compact`, and the docs now also list `clear` and `fork`, decide whether they get the board; the `MultiEdit` matcher is kept although 2.1.269's tool list no longer shows the tool; `settings sync` writes `Bash(python3.14 -I -S <home>/bin/spud *)`, `Bash(<sys.executable> -I -S <home>/bin/spud *)` and `Bash(<home>/bin/spud *)`, and `permissions.allow` in a project settings file is ignored until the folder is trusted while the hook's own allow is not; the harness refuses, from a worktree session, both `git -C <main checkout>` and Write-tool writes to shared-checkout paths ("edit the worktree copy instead"), so the recipe becomes: ledger commits on `main` before `EnterWorktree` or after `ExitWorktree keep`, and no spudagent writes a ledger file at all once the CLI is the ledger.

## Size, persona and model decision
No spudagent: every deliverable is a Spud-owned file, which Law 1 reserves to Spud, edited when Eric says go. Same shape as [[SPD-003]].

Model: Eric first asked for opus (2026-09-12, weekly Fable budget about half used), then, since a session cannot switch its own model, said to continue on fable for now; Spud runs this ticket on **fable**.

## Outcome
Rewritten by Spud on fable (Eric's word), no spudagent. `CLAUDE.md`: a new section The ledger CLI (what `spud` means, the actors, the exit codes); the session ritual on `spud board`, `card` and `member show`, with the `SessionStart` injection and a guard for a missing database; the ten laws reworded around the CLI and the hooks that refuse them; the protocol as ticket, plan, spawn, return with the exact commands, the reservation rule for retries, the `SPUD-nnn/Name (lineage, persona)` description, background by default; teams and identity with the CLI drawing names and lineages; proposals and Blocked as `proposal file|decide` and `member block`; Ledger v1 replacing Ledger v0, with `import --file` and `render --discard` for hand edits, the hooks summary and `hook.denied`; Main and worktrees with the harness's three refusals from a worktree session and the render-commit-exit recipe; the brief template on `--as <agent_id>` and `member result` before return; Reporting via `report add`; Commands. `.claude/agents/spudagent.md` rewritten the same way (The ledger, First, While working, Sub-agents, Upward channels, Finishing). Both templates keep the rendered shape and name the command that fills each section; the member template starts `planned`.

Verified: every command, flag and status in the prose checked against `spud --help` and each subcommand's help on `main` at a6f10db; `contractor` is accepted by `member new` without a config entry; the templates are not read at runtime; the suite is green after the edits (`Ran 207 tests in 92.017s` / `OK`, no bytecode, no `.spud/`).

Decisions: `SessionStart` stays `startup|resume|compact` as built, no board injection on `clear` or `fork` (the ritual's step 2 reads the board anyway); the `MultiEdit` matcher stays; the `.gitignore` line for `.spud/` ([[SPD-012]]) lands with the cutover.

Left: the second half of Done when, a ticket run after the cutover with a team that used only `spud` commands, is the cutover's acceptance and is recorded here when the first post-cutover ticket returns. Until cutover, no ticket starts: the new prose describes commands that need the database.

**Accepted 2026-09-12.** [[SPD-015]] was the first ticket run after the cutover and closes the second half of Done when. The whole run used only `spud` commands and the hooks: `ticket edit|move`, `member new` (which drew [[SPUD-015/Pompadour|Pompadour]] and computed `01`), the `PreToolUse(Agent)` check on the description `SPUD-015/Pompadour (01, engineer)` with an explicit model, `PostToolUse` binding the agent, `SessionStart` injecting the board, `member log|result` from the spudagent, `proposal file` and `proposal decide --decision create` (which made [[SPD-018]]), `member finish`, `handoff add`, `report add`, `render`. Three points the prose got right in practice: the worktree recipe (ledger committed on `main` before `EnterWorktree`, code on `worktree-spd-015-lead-hold`), the brief template (the spudagent found its brief with `member show` and never touched a ledger file), and the `Stop` hook, which held Spud's turn once for the unrecorded return exactly as written. One correction for a later ticket: the brief template's Limits line and the Sub-agents prose do not say that a background child is not killed when its parent returns, which [[SPD-015]] proved and now enforces; that edit lands when Eric merges the SPD-015 branch.
